query: In the paper, to study the XRB jet ejecta population more broadly, the researchers fit a simple powerlaw to the rest-frame emission of the approaching and receding components of MAXI J1820, excluding what?
answer:
According to the provided evidence, in the paper, to study the XRB jet ejecta population more broadly, the researchers fit a simple power-law to the rest-frame emission of the approaching and receding components of MAXI J1820, excluding regions of lower flux.

Specifically, this is evident from the following excerpt:

"The large-scale jet ejecta from MAXI J1820 are consistent with an intrinsic powerlaw flux of 𝐹𝜈 ∝ 𝑡 −3.6, with receding ejecta flux being produced much earlier in the jet rest frame despite Figure 7. Predicted MAXI J1820-like emission from the approaching (left panels) and receding (right panels) as a function of time and Γ0 for three viewing angles (𝜃v = [15, 45, 75] deg). Note the powerlaw colourscale changes for each row. Cyan dashed contours again correspond to 𝐹𝜈 = 150 μJy flux, with the white hatched region excluding regions of lower flux."

This indicates that the researchers excluded regions of lower flux when fitting a power-law to the emission data.

Would you like more details on any specific part of this finding?
